title: The online grocery class of 1999
lede: Webvan’s 10-K named its online competitors: Peapod, PDQuick and Albertsons.com, plus GrocerWorks, Safeway’s affiliate. Only the ones attached to a grocery chain lasted.

rows: Webvan
Own automated distribution centers, own vans and couriers
Benchmark, Sequoia, SOFTBANK; $375M IPO[^1]
Shut down Jul 9, 2001. Chapter 11 on Jul 13[^8]
HomeGrocer
Smaller centers (CFCs) designed for 2,500 orders a day[^3]
IPO in March 2000, reported at $288M (secondary source)[^26]
Merged into Webvan Sep 5, 2000 for about $1.04B in stock[^3]
Peapod
Online ordering tied to a grocery chain’s stores
Royal Ahold[^3]
Survived as Ahold’s online grocery business
GrocerWorks.com
Online arm of a supermarket chain
Safeway[^3]
Folded into Safeway’s own online service (not covered in our sources)
Kozmo.com
One-hour delivery of convenience goods by courier
Reported $250M–$280M raised[^24]
Ceased operations April 2001[^24]
Streamline.com
Subscription delivery to a refrigerated box at the home
Closed November 2000, citing losses and tight capital[^25]

blocks.title: Four delivery start-ups raised money in 1999 and 2000. None was operating by the end of 2001.
blocks.subtitle: Money raised by each company, and what became of it. The survivor is a later company, shown by its revenue.

items.name: Webvan
items.text: $393.3M of private preferred stock plus the $375M IPO.[^1] Shut down July 9, 2001.[^10]

items.name: HomeGrocer
items.text: IPO in March 2000, as reported by a secondary source.[^26] Merged into Webvan in September 2000 for about $1.04B in stock.[^3]

items.name: Kozmo.com
items.text: Reported total raised. Ceased operations in April 2001.[^24]

items.name: Streamline.com
items.text: IPO in June 1999. Closed in November 2000, citing losses and tight capital.[^25]

items.name: Instacart (public since 2023)
items.text: 2025 revenue, on 338.8 million orders.[^33] Webvan’s 2000 sales were $178.5M.[^3]

blocks.source: Company figures as cited. The Webvan total is the derived sum of its private rounds ($118.3M and $275.0M, net) and the gross proceeds of the 25 million shares in its prospectus[^1]. HomeGrocer’s and Kozmo’s figures are from secondary and press sources[^24][^26]. Instacart’s figure is annual revenue from its 10-K, not money raised[^33]. Peapod and GrocerWorks are left out because we have no sourced figures for them.

blocks.body: Peapod’s and GrocerWorks’ later histories are context we didn’t source in detail, so we don’t give figures for them.
